notes.read_side: Both families read the WORKING TREE, not HEAD: an uncommitted corpus edit is a legitimate observation. Record `git status --porcelain` beside the numbers.
notes.equal_mode: corpus.index.tracked_files and corpus.pointers.commit_total are change detectors, not invariants: adding a corpus file or a new commit citation moves them and must move the baseline with it (same convention as verifiers/baseline.json).
notes.zero_mode: zero-mode ids ignore `expect` at evaluation time; they are listed so the baseline names every id the script checks. A zero-mode violation exits 1 even under --no-baseline.
notes.out_of_scope_context: corpus.pointers.commit_quoted_excluded and corpus.pointers.report_pointers_other are context, not checks. The first counts `commit `<token>`` citations fully enclosed in double quotes (quoted meta-findings, e.g. corpus/lessons/round-6-aggregator-audit.md:45; live: 1). The second counts report pointers that are NOT the spec'd `(../)+` class — host-absolute, `~/`-anchored or bare (live: 24 checked, 23 absolute + 1 tilde; the earlier bare form was re-presented at landing). A double-quoted report pointer is *documented* in the script docstring as recorded context (report_pointers_quoted_detail) — live-tree shape yet to be exercised; whether the documented idiom actually fires is a round-12 question for the independent derivation.
notes.reproduce_before: Against a clone of d49dfa5 with the landed script copied in (README pre-fix): report_dead=10/19, commit_total=18, commit_nonhash=1, exit 1 — the DRIFT the round-11 edit clears. The same clone run twice is byte-identical under --json.
notes.environment: exit 2 when the target is not a git repo / corpus/README.md is unreadable; exit 3 when this file is absent and --no-baseline was not passed.
